text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.49% today to close at $151.55, capping a remarkable week-long rally that gained 10.17% in just six trading days. The spike was driven by surging oil prices—U.S. crude jumped to $107.89 per barrel and Brent to $115.22—fueled by Middle East tensions between Iran and Saudi Arabia that have raised the risk of supply disruptions. Geopolitical risk premiums in oil directly benefit major producers like ConocoPhillips, whose earnings hinge on the price they can sell crude for.

The broader energy trade has shifted decisively in favor of U.S. producers and exporters this month. Rising Middle East instability is not only pushing crude prices higher but also reshaping global energy markets in ways that benefit American oil and natural gas companies—making the energy sector itself a beneficiary of regional risk, rather than a victim of it.
